hook: Did you know that the 'heat' you feel from a chili pepper isn't actually a taste?
body: It's true! What you perceive as spicy isn't detected by your taste buds at all. Instead, compounds called capsaicinoids in peppers activate pain receptors in your mouth and throat. These are the same receptors that react to actual heat, like a burning stove. Your brain interprets this signal as a burning sensation, even though no real burning is happening. That's why milk can help: the fats in milk dissolve the capsaicin, washing it away from those pain receptors.
cta: Like this video if you've ever regretted biting into a super hot pepper!
